      - term: European Union
      - definition:
        - text: "In the EU, somatropin has been authorised since the 1980s for growth hormone replacement and short stature in specific childhood conditions, while tesamorelin has no marketing authorisation (its application was withdrawn on 21 June 2012). No centrally authorised medicine containing sermorelin, ipamorelin or CJC-1295 was found in the Union Register or EMA's data (25 September 2026), and ibutamoren (MK-677) is not an authorised medicine: its orphan designation for growth hormone deficiency (20 June 2017) is, as EMA states, not a marketing authorisation."
        - generic: "Source: Somatropin-containing medicines — Article 107 review (EMEA/H/A-107/001287) · Egrifta (tesamorelin) — withdrawal of the marketing authorisation application · Union Register of medicinal products for human use (authorised, not active and refused lists) · Download medicine data — EMA medicines data table (centrally authorised, refused, withdrawn and withdrawn-application medicines) · EU/3/17/1882 — orphan designation for ibutamoren mesilate for the treatment of growth hormone deficiency"
      - term: Portugal
      - definition:
        - text: In Portugal, no medicine containing tesamorelin, sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295 or ibutamoren (MK-677) is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (25 September 2026). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed (Decreto-Lei 95/2004).
        - generic: "Source: Infomed – base de dados de medicamentos do Infarmed (pesquisa avançada and 'Detalhes do Medicamento' pages) · Decreto-Lei n.º 95/2004, de 22 de abril – regula a prescrição e a preparação de medicamentos manipulados · Medicamentos manipulados – Inspeção de medicamentos manipulados"
      - term: Brazil
      - definition:
        - text: In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin or sermorelin was found in ANVISA's register (25 September 2026), and ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that CJC-1295 and ipamorelin products are not registered with ANVISA and that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded. Ibutamoren is not a registered medicine, and ANVISA refused the clinical-trial petitions for ibutamoren mesylate on 9 June 2026.
        - generic: "Source: Dados abertos de medicamentos registrados (DADOS_ABERTOS_MEDICAMENTOS.csv) · Documentação e Dicionário de Dados – Registros Válidos Medicamento V1 · Consultas – Medicamentos (product and substance search) · Checamos: peptídeos que prometem milagres NÃO estão registrados na Anvisa · Resolução-RE nº 2.318, de 9 de junho de 2026"
      - term: United Arab Emirates
      - definition:
        - text: In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. Somatropin is registered and dispensed as a semi-controlled drug, while no registered product containing tesamorelin, sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295 or ibutamoren was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard treats peptides as non-monographed, high-risk substances and lets novel substances of unknown risk be compounded only if monographed, part of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances (August 2026).
        - generic: "Source: Federal Decree-Law No. (28) of 2023 On the Establishment of the UAE Drug Corporation (official English translation) · Federal Decree-Law No. (38) of 2024 Governing Medical Products, Pharmacists and Pharmaceutical Establishments (official English translation) · Genotropin® 12 mg GoQuick® — EDE register entry · Registered medical product directory (Drug Directory) · DHA External Circular DHA/OUT/2026/0000867: Regulations for Handling Peptide Products in Healthcare Facilities (technical annex) · DoH Standard for Provision of Compounding Pharmacy Services (DoH/SD/HLS/PCPS/V1/2026)"
      - term: Saudi Arabia
      - definition: "Saudi context: assess exact products, indications and routes separately for tesamorelin, sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295 and ibutamoren. This review has not established Saudi registration for exact products; US compounding lists or overseas use do not establish permission."
    - paragraph: Dated to FDA's 503A category list of 14 May 2026, its Category 2 page (current as of 22 April 2026), the October 2024 advisory-committee votes, the bulks list in 21 CFR 216.23 and Drugs@FDA as checked on 24 September 2026. Absence from every list does not make a substance permitted, and FDA stopped placing newly nominated substances into categories in January 2025.
    - strong: Somatropin · tesamorelin
    - generic: FDA-approved for defined indications
    - generic: Growth-hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders; HIV-associated abdominal fat. Knowingly distributing growth hormone for other uses, anti-ageing included, is a federal offence (21 U.S.C. 333(e)).
    - strong: Sermorelin
    - generic: No approved product on the market
    - generic: Approved as Geref in 1990 and 1997, discontinued in 2008, approvals withdrawn in 2009 at the maker's request; FDA found in 2013 that this was not for safety or effectiveness reasons. In no 503A category.
    - strong: Ibutamoren (MK-677)
    - generic: 503A and 503B Category 2
    - generic: FDA cites a heart-failure signal that stopped a hip-fracture trial early. The advisory committee voted 13 to 1 against adding it to the bulks list (October 2024).
    - strong: Ipamorelin · CJC-1295
    - generic: Withdrawn 503A nominations
    - generic: FDA lists both among Category 2 nominations that were withdrawn, citing serious adverse events; ipamorelin remains in 503B Category 2. The committee voted 0 to 12, with one abstention, against listing ipamorelin (October 2024).
    - strong: GHRP-2 · GHRP-6
    - generic: 503A Category 3
    - generic: Nominated without adequate support for FDA to evaluate; both in 503B Category 2.
    - strong: IGF-1 LR3
    - generic: No approved product, no category
    - generic: Named in a 2020 FDA warning letter, with CJC-1295, ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and MK-677, as ineligible for the 503A exemptions.
    - paragraph: The 503A bulks list holds six substances, none on this axis. Check the live lists before any conversation about compounding.
